tenures.bio:
Born in Bolt West Virginia, the Corporal got his start in the real world by beating up weaker children in school. The neighborhood bully was the Corporals name to fame. Breaking childrens bikes and pushing children off the sidewalk in front of traffic was one of his most favorite things growing up.

But that all changed when he enlisted in the United States Marine Corp. The Corporal fell right at home when he was placed in Special Forces. To him, there was nothing like being sent off to foreign countries to assassinate non-Americans. The best part of the ordeal was that he was doing it in the name of the good ole US of A. This career gave the Corporal an unsurpassed feeling of pride seeing as he was killing people in the name of patriotism. For 10 years, the Corporal became the most ruthless assassin the United States Marine Corp. ever trained. 

This would all end however. After the 1993 Russian blood bath incident, the Corporal was asked to step down as the captain of the S.S.A.R.C. for publicly admitting to the Russian media that he enjoyed listening to their fallen comrades scream while he cut of every left ear of theirs. He then pulled the ear-skinned necklace that he created from the fallen comrades detached lobes, and laughed as they began to scream in anger. 

The Corporal enjoyed the need for confrontation so much that instead of retiring from service, he transferred from military duty to the world of corrections. There he would find an even more compassioned love for sadistic-ness as the chief warden at the infamous Attica State Prison. For the first time, his ruthlessness could be done out in the open and the lack of compassion the public had in the prison industry, made the Corporal an even bigger public name. His tactics were not only ruthless and heartless, but the large majority of American citizens gave praise for the way he executed inmates for their crimes. 

The Corporal became hated amongst the inmate population, but respected amongst the uniform staff. Law enforcement agencies began using the Corporal as the standard way of doing things in the inner cities across the United States. The Corporal had found yet another perfect fit for his thirst of giving pain.

It was not until 2000 that the Corporal became interested in the professional world of wrestling. His antics for cruelty made him a fan favorite no matter how ruthless and disloyal he was to those who professed good as their handle in the ring. The Corporal made a world-renowned name for himself in several small structured wrestling agencies. It was within 2 years that the Corporal handily began to dismantle small wrestling organization by literally destroying their competition in the name of MARTIAL LAW.

The Corporal would conquer twelve wrestling federations before entering four federations that would mold his career as the cruelest and most sadistic name in wrestling. The TWF, UWF, HCWF and GIWF would welcome the Corporal with open arms solely for the purpose of humiliating the jobbers of professional wrestling. 

The Corporal would enter the most famous stable in wrestling history 'The Youngbloods' and as their chief enforcer the Corporal could blindly torment all that dared to stand in the Corporals way of enforcing Martial Law on those who apposed the YB way of family business.

 Having the slogan, Dont take it PERSONAL JUST TAKE IT CORPORAL STYLE! Corporal Punishment has created a fan base that resembles a neo-nazi movement. Instead of spreading racism and bigotry, the Corporal fan base spreads the thirst for pain and devastation. Known as Punishment-ites The Corporals loyal fan base travel far and abroad to ensure that when the Corporal enters the ring, the Corporal has thousands watching his back. And thousands ready to retaliate at his beckoned word. Thus why the Corporal is literally the most dangerous man in wrestling PERIOD.

tenures.bio:
Once a hardened criminal wrestling under the name of Mr. Meaner (yes, he wrestled in the GIWF under this name) Kazee switched to who he is now after nearly losing his daughter and estranged wife in a house fire.  

He is a former championship amateur wrestler and has retained much of that knowledge.  Knowing that he would never be strong, fast, or big, he continued on and learned submission maneuvers.  While Kazee may not be fast, he has surprising quickness which can reverse a maneuver in an instant.

'The Common Man' Ezra Kazee is exactly what he says he is.  Just a common man who has been given some great opportunities and will do whatever he can for his fans, whom he calls the Commonwealth.  He lives by the idea of fairness, sportsmanship, and being the best person possible.  His constant belief in these things gives the audience a refreshing sense and earns him the respect of friend and foe alike.

However, with recent events, he has lost his mind so to speak, and now seems to have split personalities.  He has reverted back to Mr. Meaner as well as a new persona named Fizbane the Fabulous.  How does this all work out?  Just keep watching and I'm sure you'll find out.

Under his own name he lost a four-way for the number-one contendership to the Alias Championship, won by Easton Hall, on ReVolution 120 (22 February 2007), and entered the Dual Halo finale at Culture Shock on 11 March 2007, billed "No longer under the mask of Ember"; Jason Snow's Snake Eyes eliminated him after Tony Gamble pushed him into it. Held to that contract by C.P. Cantrell, he came back on ReVolution 175 (8 October 2008), lost to Enemigo III by count-out when he walked out, then lay down for the pin when Cantrell ordered the match restarted; PRIME's news of 14 October 2008 advertised his debut at Great American Nightmare and noted he had already competed "under the mask of Ember (despite not seeming to realize it at the time)", and there, on 19 October, Cantrell put him in a handicap match against DUI, and Colby Korver lay down for his pin. In 2009 he made peace with Jonathon Winters over the Ember years (ReVolution 184, 28 January) and lost a 5 Star Championship ladder match to High Flyer (ReVolution 186, 18 February); he gave up his late Dual Halo draw for a match with Hunter Sabuani, lost it at Culture Shock on 13 March, entered the Dual Halo first the next night and was pinned by the returning Jason Natas. At ReVolution 200 (8 July) he was the sole survivor of Power Play's fourth match, pinning Karina Wolfenden last, then eliminated Natas again in the closing battle royal and lasted to its final three, which carried him an Intense Championship shot. He lost an I Quit match to Natas at Colossus VI (16 August) under terms Natas set, that the man who quit would leave PRIME, and on ReVolution 204 (2 September) turned the result on Natas, who had said the words first. He lost the three-way in which Tony Gamble took the 5 Star Championship from Jason Snow (9 September) and a 5 Star Championship challenge to Gamble at Great American Nightmare (18 October), was made to lie down for Tyler Nelson in a tag match on ReVolution 213 and so joined Nelson's Army, and was last seen losing to Troy Douglas at King of Kings on 20 December 2009. A recovered alcoholic, White Wolf is apparently now back into his intense habbits of snapping at everyone around him.

identity.note: The GIWF's John Tenzan record is folded in here. "John Tenzan" appears in one document only, the lineage's own Hall of Fame page: "The Dreamwarriors -- The Sandman & John Tenzan (Inducted December 29th, 1999)", "Achievements: GIWF World Tag Team Champions, IWF World Tag Team Champions (x2)". That page names the Dreamwarriors' second member, and every other record of the team names him John Constantine. The GIWF card of 1 September 1999 reads "the Sandman and John Constantine, collectively known as the Dreamwarriors". The card of 6 April 1999 reads "John Constantine and Sandman of the Dreamwarriors". The IWF's Christmas Clash recap reads "the Dream Warriors consisting of John Constantine & Sandman", and its tag-team rankings list "Dream Warriors (Sandman/Constantine)". The UWF's all-time roster (captured 27 August 2006) lists "John Constantine (Dreamwarriors w/ Sandman)" and "Sandman (Dreamwarriors w/ John Constantine)". The GIWF's 1999 awards ceremony inducted "The Dream Warriors" that same December. The surname on the Hall of Fame page is Tenzan's. One IWF handler-bio page lists that handler's characters as "Akira, Tenzan, Constantine and The Sandman", and the same 1999 ceremony lists the Warrior Clan as "Akira and The Dream Warriors". Yoshihiro Tenzan (yoshihiro-tenzan), Akira's brother from Nagoya, is a different man and his record is untouched. The IWF's 1999 roster lists "John Constantine" and "Yoshihiro Tenzan" on separate lines, as does the UWF's all-time roster, and the GIWF's 1999 cards have "Yoshirio Tenzan" leading Akira to the ring while the Dreamwarriors wrestle as Constantine and Sandman. The sources disagree on the name, so "John Tenzan" is kept as an aka. Whether this record and the IWF's own John Constantine are one character is not decided here; that record carries a presumed portrayal edge.

name: Flammable
notes: Misled Youth's original tag team with Freak: billed "Flammable and Freak" in the stable's debut on Suicide of 3 April 1999, a falls-count-anywhere win over the Mighty Israelites in which Flammable's tiger driver pinned Shylock in the back of the arena (/promotions/giwf/archive/suicide-1999-04-03.html); named among the brawlers as "Flammable and Freak of Misled Youth" on Global of 6 April (/promotions/giwf/archive/global-1999-04-06.html); beat the Thompson Boys with Freak, no disqualification, on Global of 28 April; lost the rematch to the Mighty Israelites at Fear the Raine on 1 May 1999 (/promotions/giwf/archive/fear-the-raine.html); walked out with Freak and Pyro as Misled Youth on Global of 11 May; still at ringside with the stable through Global of 15 June 1999. In the stable's own roleplay posted 2 June 1999 (/promotions/giwf/archive/misled-youth-stable-wars-tape-review-1999-06-02.html) he reviews the Stable Wars tape with Freak, Mad Jack Manson, Pyro and the Iron Priest, coaching each on what they should have done, sets out the stable's title standings and lays down its challenges for Sunday Afternoon Suicide.
caption: Teamed with Freak in Misled Youth's debut win over the Mighty Israelites on 3 April 1999 and through that spring, then studied the Stable Wars tape with the whole stable as its strategist in June 1999.
